porbos.title: After Makkah, the Wind of Arabia • The Shadow of Rome • This Time, Naming the Destination • The Race of Giving • Those Without Mounts • The Day of Departure, ‘Ali’s Hurt • The Hardship of the Road • Past al-Hijr • The Spring of Tabuk • The Romans Did Not Come

blocks.0: After Makkah, the Wind of Arabia
blocks.1: Makkah has been conquered. The battles of Hunayn and Ta’if are over. A new wind is now blowing across the heart of Arabia. The tribes that had been sitting far away watching, to see who would win the fight between Quraysh and Muhammad, now find nothing left to watch. People have begun coming into the shade of Islam in crowds. Ten years of unbroken fighting. Badr, Uhud, the Trench, Khaybar, Makkah, Hunayn. For the first time the people of Madinah have found a chance to catch their breath. They have returned home, put their hands to their orchards, and begun counting up the harvest to bring in. But one thorn still remained, the farthest, the biggest. Rome. A year earlier, on the plain of Mu’tah, three thousand Muslims had stood before the vast army of Rome. Three commanders had been martyred. By the strategy of Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) the army had come back. But the emperor of Rome, Caesar Heraclius, could not forget that event. To him it was now not merely a battle, but a danger on the frontier. If the tribes of Arabia that have begun to speak of independence hear this story of Rome’s humiliation, who will guard Rome’s borders?{{1}}
blocks.2: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} understood all of this. He had no room to sit back in the joy of the conquest of Makkah. The danger ahead had to be stopped before it reached the door.
blocks.4: In the air of Madinah there was only one talk then. That Ghassan was shoeing its horses. In every home in Madinah there was this fear. ‘Umar (RA) has said,
blocks.5: We used to say among ourselves that Ghassan was shoeing its horses to attack us.{{1}}
blocks.6: The fear was not baseless. The Nabataean merchants who came to Madinah from Syria bringing oil brought news. Heraclius had gathered a monstrous army of forty thousand soldiers. He had paid the soldiers a year’s salary in advance. With them the Arab Christian tribes of Lakhm and Judham. At the head of the army, famous commanders of Rome. Their advance party had already reached Balqa’. That very day a terror spread through Madinah that no one could forget, day or night. At any unfamiliar sound it seemed that the Romans had arrived.{{1}}
blocks.7: And inside Madinah, the time was the most difficult of all. After ten years of continuous war, a little peace had come for the first time. The dates were ripening, and on these dates rested the livelihood of the people of Madinah for the whole year. Leaving the orchards was not easy. The heat of Arabia was fierce then. It felt as if fire rained from the sky, sparks leapt from the ground. The journey too was very long. Nearly eight hundred miles, mostly harsh desert. Mounts were few. And as for the Romans they were to face, the Muslims had no idea at all of their methods of warfare.{{1}}
blocks.8: And the time was the most difficult of all. Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA) has spoken of those days,
blocks.9: The Prophet {{1}} set out on this expedition in the midst of fierce heat. Ahead lay a distant journey, endless desert, and an enormous number of enemies.{{2}}
blocks.10: The Prophet {{1}} calculated. If the Romans came to Madinah first, then all the spread that Islam had gained through years of toil and sweat would be wasted in an instant. After the storm of Hunayn, Jahiliyyah, thrashing on its deathbed, would take courage again. And the hypocrites within, who until now had been sitting with daggers in hand behind the back, would join hands with the Romans and plunge the knife into the back. So the decision was made: before they come, we will go.{{2}}
blocks.11: Some tasks are never done if one waits for good days. Let the heat ease, let the harvest come in, let the road become easy, let companions increase; such a day does not come.
blocks.13: The Prophet’s {{1}} rule was to conceal the destination before setting out for battle. He would be going in one direction and speak of another. This time he did not do so. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.14: The Prophet {{1}} laid the matter openly before the Muslims, so that they could make full preparation. He also told them which direction he was going.{{2}}
blocks.15: The Companions were so many that not everyone’s name was written in any register. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.16: Whoever wished to stay absent would think that unless revelation from Allah came, the matter would remain hidden.{{1}}
blocks.17: The announcement to prepare for war went out in every direction. To the other tribes of Arabia, to the people of Makkah too. At this time a part of Surah al-Tawbah was revealed. The Muslims were urged to jihad. The Prophet {{1}} encouraged them to spend the best part of their wealth in the way of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.18: The Qur’an puts that call this way,
blocks.20: O believers! What is the matter with you that when you were told to go out in the way of Allah, you became weighed down and clung to the earth? Are you content with the life of this world in place of the Hereafter? (If so, then remember) against the Hereafter the enjoyment of this worldly life is very little.{{1}}
blocks.21: And what will happen if they do not go, the Qur’an has said at once,
blocks.23: If you do not go out, Allah will punish you with a painful punishment and will bring another people in your place, and you cannot harm Him in the least. Allah has complete power over all things.{{1}}
blocks.24: And the call to go had come for everyone, with no exemption to sit at home, in every state, light or heavy. The Qur’an puts that call this way,
blocks.26: (Set out for jihad) go forth, whether you are light or heavy, and strive with your lives and wealth in the way of Allah. If you have understanding, this is better for you.{{1}}
blocks.27: As for those who stood behind the shield of excuses, the Qur’an has also pulled out what was in their hearts: had the road been near and the profit in hand, these very people would have walked first of all.
blocks.29: Had there been immediate worldly gain in sight and the journey been of moderate length, they (that is, the hypocrites) would surely have followed you. But this hard road seemed too far to them. Now they will swear by Allah, saying, if we had been able, we would surely have gone out with you. They are destroying themselves, and Allah knows well that they are liars.{{1}}
blocks.30: Before setting out on the desert road, the biggest obstacle is not the enemy but the pull of the earth. ‘Weighed down and clung to the earth,’ this picture of the Qur’an we recognise. Bed, shade, comfort pin us to the ground too.
blocks.32: The call has come, now the preparation. An army of thirty thousand had to be assembled. The Muslims had never before set out with so large a force, and yet mounts were few, provisions few, weapons few. That is why in history this army is named Jaysh al-‘Usrah, the Army of Hardship. And to bear that hardship a race of giving broke out in Madinah. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah (RA) says, while the army was being equipped ‘Uthman (RA) came with a thousand dinars. He poured them into the lap of the Prophet {{1}}. ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) says,
blocks.33: I saw the Prophet {{1}} turning the dinars over and over in his lap and saying, after today, whatever ‘Uthman does, no harm will come to him. He said it twice.{{2}}
blocks.34: This is not a licence for sin. It is a declaration of trust in one who knows how to pour out everything for Allah. ‘Umar (RA) says, the Prophet {{1}} commanded sadaqah. That day I had some wealth in my hand. I said to myself, if I can ever surpass Abu Bakr, it is today. I brought half of my wealth. The Prophet {{2}} asked, what have you left for your family? I said, the same amount. Then Abu Bakr came with everything he had.
blocks.35: The Prophet {{1}} asked, Abu Bakr, what have you left for your family? He said, I have left Allah and His Messenger for them.{{2}}
blocks.36: ‘Umar (RA) said, by Allah, I will never be able to surpass him in anything. And those who had nothing at all to give? Abu Mas‘ud (RA) says,
blocks.37: When we were commanded to give sadaqah, we used to labour for wages, carrying loads on our backs. Abu ‘Aqil came with half a sa‘. Another came with more than that. The hypocrites said, Allah has no need of this one’s sadaqah; and that man has brought it only to show off.{{1}}
blocks.38: The Qur’an answered them this way,
blocks.40: (Such hypocrites are) those who find fault with the believers who give sadaqah willingly, and also with those who find nothing but the fruit of their own labour. For this they ridicule them. Allah ridicules them in return. For them a painful punishment is prepared.{{1}}
blocks.41: For the big giver the excuse of ‘showing off,’ and for the small giver the excuse of ‘trivial,’ is always ready. The one who gives nothing, his mouth runs the most. The real bargain behind this giving the Qur’an has put this way,
blocks.43: In fact Allah has bought from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for the Garden being theirs. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. This is a true promise, which Allah has taken upon Himself in the Torah and the Injil, and in the Qur’an too. And who is more faithful to his promise than Allah? So rejoice in the bargain you have made with Allah, and that is the great success.{{1}}
blocks.44: Those who poured out everything that day knew they had not entered a business of loss. They had struck a bargain, whose buyer is Allah.
blocks.46: In the midst of this crowd of giving there was another group, who had nothing to give; they had only the longing to go. No mount had come their way, so they have no excuse, they have yearning. Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) says, his companions sent him to the Prophet {{1}} to ask for mounts. The Prophet {{2}} was angry at that time, Abu Musa (RA) did not notice. He said,
blocks.47: By Allah, I cannot give you anything to ride.{{1}}
blocks.48: Abu Musa (RA) went back heartbroken. He feared that the Prophet {{1}} might be displeased with him. A little later Bilal (RA) called out, where is ‘Abdullah ibn Qays? The Prophet {{2}} is calling. He went and saw six camels. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.49: These two and these two and these two, six camels in pairs, just bought from Sa‘d. Take them and go to your companions.{{1}}
blocks.50: Allah Himself had drawn the boundary of excuses,
blocks.52: There is no blame on the weak (for not going to jihad), nor on the sick, nor on those who have nothing to spend, as long as they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no ground of complaint against the doers of good. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.53: And for those who needed this mount, the Qur’an has preserved even their tears,
blocks.55: Nor is there any blame on those who came to you in the hope that you would arrange some mount for them, and you said, I have no mount to give you, whereupon, in grief at having nothing to spend, they turned back with tears flowing from their eyes.{{1}}
blocks.56: They did not weep because they got no mount; they wept because the reward slipped away. Though there would have been no sin on them even if they did not go, their eyes flooded with grief at the lost opportunity. When did our eyes last grow wet for something that no one would have held us to account for if we had not done it?
blocks.58: The preparation was complete. On the day of departure the Prophet {{1}} left ‘Ali (RA) behind in Madinah. ‘Ali’s (RA) heart grew heavy. There was no battle in which he had not stood beside the Prophet {{2}}; only this time was he left behind. The hypocrites taunted, he has been left because he had become a burden.{{3}}
blocks.59: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) says, ‘Ali (RA) said to the Prophet {{1}},
blocks.60: Are you leaving me among the children and women? The Prophet {{1}} said, are you not pleased that your standing with me will be like the standing of Harun with Musa? Except that there is no prophet after me.{{2}}
blocks.61: Two things in one sentence. One for ‘Ali, of love. The other for the whole ummah, of boundary. The comparison with Harun (AS) is of responsibility, not of prophethood. To make that clear came the last part of the sentence: there is no prophet after me.
blocks.63: The moment they set out on the road, the true face of hardship appeared. Eighteen men took turns on one camel. Driven by hunger they chewed tree leaves, and their lips swelled. When water ran out they slaughtered a camel and drank the water in its belly.{{1}}
blocks.64: At one point the people were faint with hunger. They said to the Prophet {{1}}, allow us to slaughter our camels and eat, and we will use the oil too. The Prophet {{2}} said, do it. Then ‘Umar (RA) came and said,
blocks.65: O Messenger of Allah, if they do this, the mounts will be fewer. Rather, tell them to bring what remains of their food, then pray for blessing upon it. Perhaps Allah will do something through that.{{1}}
blocks.66: A leather dining-cloth was spread. One brought a handful of corn, another a handful of dates, another a piece of bread. Altogether very little. The Prophet {{1}} prayed for blessing. Then he said, fill your vessels. Not a single vessel of the soldiers remained that they had not filled. All ate to their fill, and still food was left over. Then the Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.67: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that I am the Messenger of Allah. Any servant who stands before Allah with these two, without doubt, will not be shut out from the Garden.{{1}}
blocks.68: ‘Umar’s (RA) advice is a lesson of crisis. Not lamenting over what is not there, but bringing together what is there in one place. A handful from each; together, the stomach of the whole army.
blocks.70: On the way lay al-Hijr. The settlement of Thamud, the people of Salih (AS). Those who had built houses by cutting into the mountains. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) says, as they passed there the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.71: Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves; lest what happened to them happen to you too. But if you enter weeping, that is another matter.{{1}}
blocks.72: Today we go to see ancient ruins. We take photos, laugh, sit down and open food packets. The Prophet {{1}} walked on, his head covered with his cloak.
blocks.74: Coming near Tabuk the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.75: Tomorrow, in sha’ Allah, you will reach the spring of Tabuk. But not before midday. Whoever arrives first, until I come let him not put his hand in the water there.{{1}}
blocks.76: Mu‘adh (RA) says, when we arrived we found two had already got there. The spring was thin as a shoelace, water seeping out drop by drop. The Prophet {{1}} asked, did you touch its water? They said, yes. He rebuked them. Then the people, filling their cupped hands, gathered a little water bit by bit in a vessel. The Prophet {{2}} washed his face and hands in it, then poured the water back into the spring.
blocks.77: The spring poured out water in a rush, or he said, a great deal of water. The people drank. Then the Prophet {{1}} said, Mu‘adh, if you live long, you will see this place filled with gardens.{{2}}
blocks.78: Another warning of that same night. Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi (RA) says, on reaching Tabuk the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.79: Tonight a fierce wind will blow. Let no one stand up. Whoever has a camel with him, let him tie it down.{{1}}
blocks.80: We tied down our camels. At night a fierce wind came. One man stood up. The wind lifted him and threw him down on the mountain of the Tayy tribe. The reason for the order about the spring’s water, ‘do not touch it until I come,’ became clear later. The Prophet’s {{1}} displeasure toward those who had touched it first also says, an order has a reason. The reason is not always understood at once.
blocks.82: The army pitched camp on the plain of Tabuk. The Prophet {{1}} gave a speech; much in few words. He called to the good of this world and the Hereafter, gave warning too, gave glad tidings too. The morale of the Muslim army rose still higher. Meanwhile when the Romans heard that the Prophet {{2}} had arrived with an army of thirty thousand, fear wrapped itself around them like a snake. No one advanced. They scattered and dispersed inside their own country.{{3}}
blocks.83: There was no battle. But the fruits of this silent victory came one after another. The ruler of Aylah, Yuhanna ibn Ru’bah, came and made a treaty, agreed to pay jizyah. The people of Jarba’ and Adhruh also came and paid jizyah. The Prophet {{1}} gave Yuhanna a letter. It began, this is a memorial of peace. On sea and land, the responsibility for their boats and caravans lies with Allah and His Prophet. Abu Humayd (RA) says,
blocks.84: The king of Aylah presented the Prophet {{1}} with a white mule, put a cloak on him, and the Prophet {{2}} gave him a written agreement for their seacoast.{{3}}
blocks.85: Meanwhile Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) set out with four hundred and twenty horsemen toward Ukaydir, the ruler of Dumat al-Jandal. As he went the Prophet {{1}} said, you will find him hunting a nilgai (blue bull). On a moonlit night a nilgai was rubbing its horns on the palace gate. Ukaydir went out to hunt. Khalid (RA) seized him and brought him to the Prophet {{2}}. In return for his life he gave two thousand camels, eight hundred helmets, four hundred coats of mail and four hundred spears, along with an acknowledgement of jizyah.{{3}}
blocks.86: Not every victory comes by the sword. Sometimes victory means the enemy not coming forward. Standing firm is then the work itself.

porbos.title: The Pass on the Way Back • Taba and Uhud • Left Behind • Excuses and the Truth • Fifty Nights • Good News at Dawn • Conspiracy in a Mosque’s Wrapping

blocks.0: The Pass on the Way Back
blocks.1: On the way back there was a mountain pass. The herald called out, the Prophet {{1}} has taken the pass, let no one come by that road. ‘Ammar and Hudhayfah (RA) were leading the Prophet’s {{2}} camel; one holding the rein, the other driving it from behind. Suddenly a band of men with cloth wound round their faces came upon them on mounts. ‘Ammar (RA) began striking at the faces of their mounts. The Prophet {{3}} said, go on, go on.{{4}}
blocks.2: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) later revealed the number while speaking with a man of al-‘Aqabah. Abu al-Tufayl (RA) says, the man asked, for Allah’s sake, how many were the Companions of al-‘Aqabah? Hudhayfah (RA) said,
blocks.3: We were told that they were fourteen. If you are one of them, then fifteen. I bear witness by Allah that twelve of them are at war with Allah and His Messenger in the life of this world and on the day the witnesses will stand. The remaining three were given an excuse; they had said, we did not hear the herald’s call, nor did we know the intention of the people.{{1}}
blocks.4: The Prophet {{1}} had told Hudhayfah (RA) their names one by one. Among the Companions he was therefore the keeper of the Messenger’s secrets. The Qur’an puts that plot this way,
blocks.6: They swear by Allah that they did not say such-and-such. Yet they certainly said the word of disbelief and fell into disbelief after their acceptance of Islam. They intended something which they could not achieve.{{1}}
blocks.7: Ahead, the vast army of Rome. Behind, the people from inside the house. The blow was not expected from there, yet from that very place came the attempt at a blow.
blocks.9: The moment the walls of Madinah came into sight, the name of the beloved city was on the Prophet’s {{1}} lips. Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi (RA) says,
blocks.10: We were returning from the expedition of Tabuk. As we came near Madinah the Prophet {{1}} said, this is Taba, and this is Uhud, a mountain that loves us and we love it.{{2}}
blocks.11: Then he reminded his companions of those who had not been able to come along. Anas (RA) says, coming near Madinah the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.12: There are some people in Madinah who were with you on every road you travelled and every valley you crossed. The Companions said, O Messenger of Allah, they are in Madinah! He said, yes, in Madinah. A valid excuse has held them back.{{1}}
blocks.13: Here is the difference between a valid excuse and a pretext. The heart of one with a valid excuse walks along with the travellers. The heart of one with a pretext sits in Madinah already. From the outside the two look alike. Allah knows the inner matters, and the Prophet {{1}} could recognise where the heart was.
blocks.15: Those held back by valid excuses are on one side. On the other side, three who had no excuse; they had only putting off, day after day. Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA). He had been present at the pledge on the night of al-‘Aqabah. Except for Badr, he had missed no expedition with the Prophet {{1}}. He himself has said,
blocks.16: I was never so strong and well-off as I was at that time. By Allah, never before had two mounts been gathered with me at once; for that very expedition they were gathered.{{1}}
blocks.17: Then began those small returns. He said,
blocks.18: Every morning I would go out to prepare with them. I would come back having done nothing. I would say to myself, I am able. In this way, by dragging on, the people’s hurry reached its peak. The Prophet {{1}} and the Muslims set out, and my preparation remained at nothing done at all.{{2}}
blocks.19: Ka‘b (RA) thought, in a day or two I will get ready and catch up with them. Again in the morning he went, came back. Again he went, again he returned. By then they were far away. Meanwhile, on reaching Tabuk, the Prophet {{1}}, sitting among the Companions, suddenly asked,
blocks.20: What did Ka‘b do? A man of Banu Salimah said, O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and the thought of adorning himself have held him back. Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) said, how wrong a thing you have said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing about him but good. The Prophet {{1}} remained silent.{{2}}
blocks.21: Big mistakes do not usually happen in a day. Not today, tomorrow; they happen from the sum of these small returns. And the loveliest trap is that very sentence: I am able. Being able and doing are not the same thing.
blocks.23: The Prophet {{1}} returned. When he came back from a journey he would first go to the mosque and pray two rak‘ahs, then sit for the people. That day too it was so. Ka‘b (RA) says, hearing news of his return, many lies came into my mind. What shall I say tomorrow to be saved from his anger? I was consulting also the wise people of my house. Then,
blocks.24: When it was said that the Prophet {{1}} had arrived, the falsehood left my mind. I understood that I could never get out of this with a lie. So I resolved to tell the truth.{{2}}
blocks.25: Those who had stayed behind began coming and presenting their excuses and swearing oaths. They numbered a little over eighty. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}} accepted from them what was outward, took their pledge, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner secrets to Allah.{{2}}
blocks.27: What would happen after returning, the Qur’an had already said in advance this way,
blocks.29: (O Muslims!) When you return (from Tabuk) to them, they will present (various) excuses to you. (O Prophet!) Tell them, do not present excuses. We will never believe you. Allah has informed us well about your condition. And in the future Allah will see your conduct, and His Messenger too. Then you will be returned to the One who knows all that is hidden and manifest. Then He will inform you of everything you used to do.{{1}}
blocks.30: The Qur’an speaks of those people this way,
blocks.32: Those who were left behind (from the Tabuk expedition) rejoiced at sitting (in their homes) after the departure of the Messenger of Allah. And striving in the way of Allah with their lives and wealth was disliked by them. They said, do not go out in this heat. Say, the fire of Hell is fiercer in heat. If only they understood!{{1}}
blocks.33: The Qur’an has told their end too,
blocks.35: So let them laugh a little (in the world). Then they will weep much (in the Hereafter). For this is the recompense of what they had earned.{{1}}
blocks.36: And about the mistake of granting permission that the Prophet {{1}} himself once made, a word from Allah came as well. Even the manner of the rebuke is so gentle: first forgiveness, then the question,
blocks.38: (O Prophet!) Allah has forgiven you. Why did you give them permission (not to join the jihad) before it became clear to you who were truthful, and before you knew well who were liars?{{1}}
blocks.39: The announcement of forgiveness before even asking for forgiveness. Such a gentle way of correcting a loved one is rarely seen. The same picture among the desert-village people outside Madinah. The Qur’an has kept that too, this way,
blocks.41: And those making excuses from among the desert-dwellers also came, so that they might be exempted (from jihad). And (in this way) those who had lied to Allah and His Messenger all sat back. For those of them who have (completely) disbelieved there is a painful punishment.{{1}}
blocks.42: About those who, though rich, had asked for exemption, the Qur’an has said,
blocks.44: The complaint is indeed against those who ask you for exemption although they are wealthy. They are pleased to be with the women who stay behind. Allah has sealed their hearts. So they do not know the real truth.{{1}}
blocks.45: On the opposite side of all this were those who set out on their own. The Qur’an speaks of them this way,
blocks.47: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their lives and wealth. For them are all kinds of good, and they are the successful. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the great success.{{1}}
blocks.48: Then Ka‘b (RA) went forward. He gave salaam. The Prophet {{1}} smiled, the smile of an angry man. He said, come. Ka‘b (RA) walked up and sat in front. The Prophet {{2}} asked,
blocks.49: What kept you back? Had you not bought a mount?{{1}}
blocks.51: Yes, I had bought one. By Allah, had I sat before anyone else in the world but you, I would have come out of his anger with some excuse. I have been given the gift of argument. But by Allah, I know that if I satisfy you today with a lie, Allah will soon make you displeased with me. And if I tell the truth, you will be angry with me, yet I hope for Allah’s forgiveness in it. No, by Allah, I had no excuse.{{1}}
blocks.53: This one has spoken the truth. Get up, until Allah decides about you.{{1}}
blocks.54: The people of Banu Salimah rebuked him so much that Ka‘b (RA) felt like going back and calling himself a liar. He asked, has anyone else done as I did? It was said, two: Murarah ibn al-Rabi‘ and Hilal ibn Umayyah. Both are righteous men, they took part in Badr, there is a model in them. Hearing the names, he did not go back. Ka‘b (RA) saw that by lying one is released before people; not before Allah.
blocks.56: The Prophet {{1}} forbade it: of all those who stayed behind, no one was to speak with only these three. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.57: People began avoiding us, they changed toward us. The very earth became unfamiliar to me. The place I knew was no longer that place.{{1}}
blocks.58: Thus passed fifty nights. His two companions sat at home weeping. Ka‘b (RA) was the youngest, the strongest. He would go to prayer, wander in the markets, no one spoke. After the prayer he would come to the Prophet’s {{1}} gathering and give salaam. He says,
blocks.59: I would say to myself, did his lips move in answer to my salaam or not? Then I would pray close by and steal a glance. When I turned to my prayer he would turn to me, and when I turned toward him he would turn his face away.{{1}}
blocks.60: One day this silence became unbearable. Ka‘b (RA) climbed over the wall of the garden of his cousin Abu Qatadah (RA) and went inside. He gave salaam. No answer came. He said,
blocks.61: I said, Abu Qatadah, for Allah’s sake, do you not know that I love Allah and His Messenger? He stayed silent. I said it again. Again silence. The third time I said it. He said, Allah and His Messenger know best. My two eyes overflowed. I went back, climbing over the wall.{{1}}
blocks.62: Another day in the market of Madinah a Syrian trader was searching, who is Ka‘b ibn Malik? People pointed with a finger. He handed over a letter from the king of Ghassan. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.63: In the letter was written, I have learned that your companion has wronged you. Allah has not placed you in a place of humiliation and neglect. Come over to us, we will console you. After reading the letter I said, this too is a trial. Then I went to the oven and burned the letter in it.{{1}}
blocks.64: When forty nights had passed, a messenger of the Prophet {{1}} came: stay apart from your wife. Divorce? No, do not even go near her. Ka‘b (RA) sent his wife to her father’s house. Hilal’s (RA) wife sought permission to serve his aged body. The Prophet {{2}} gave it, on one condition: he must not go near her.{{3}}
blocks.65: This boycott was punishment. And also treatment. The door was kept open. The ban was only on three. The time was limited, fifty nights. The Prophet {{1}} had given permission to the wife to serve Hilal’s (RA) aged body. When we abandon someone, do we keep the door open for return? And the letter from Ghassan. When one’s own people turn their faces away, the sweet call that comes from outside is then the most dangerous. Ka‘b (RA) threw it into the oven right then.
blocks.67: The fifty nights were complete. After praying Fajr, Ka‘b (RA) sat on the roof of his house. The earth was wide, yet narrow for him. His own life was narrow too. At that moment a call came floating from the top of Mount Sal‘,
blocks.69: He fell into prostration. He understood that release had come. A horseman galloped. A man of the Aslam tribe climbed the mountain and shouted. Ka‘b (RA) says, the voice arrived faster than the horse. The one who gave the glad tidings, I took off my two garments and put them on him. By Allah, that day I had nothing but those two. Borrowing two garments, I put them on and set out toward the Prophet {{1}}. People came in groups to congratulate, may Allah’s acceptance of your repentance be blessed. Ka‘b (RA) says,
blocks.70: I entered the mosque. The Prophet {{1}} was sitting, with people around. Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydillah got up and came running, shook my hand, congratulated me. By Allah, no one else of the Muhajirun stood up for me. I will never forget this act of Talhah.{{2}}
blocks.71: Then he came face to face with the Prophet {{1}}. His face was shining with joy. He said,
blocks.72: Receive the glad tidings of the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you.{{1}}
blocks.73: Ka‘b (RA) asked, is this from you, or from Allah? The Prophet {{1}} said, no, from Allah. Then Ka‘b (RA) said, as part of my repentance I want to give all my wealth as sadaqah to Allah and His Messenger. The Prophet {{2}} said, keep some, that is better for you. Ka‘b (RA) said, then I keep my share in Khaybar. Then he said,
blocks.74: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has saved me only because of truth. Part of my repentance is that as long as I live, I will say nothing but the truth.{{1}}
blocks.75: For those who had been with him on that hard journey, the glad tidings of the Qur’an had come earlier,
blocks.77: In fact Allah turned with mercy to the Prophet and to the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who stayed with the Prophet in a hard moment, when the hearts of a party of them were about to waver. Then Allah turned with mercy to their condition. Surely He is Most Kind to them, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.78: The Qur’an speaks of these three this way,
blocks.80: And to the three as well (Allah turned with mercy) whose matter had been postponed. Until, when the earth, for all its vastness, became narrow for them, their own lives became unbearable for them, and they realised that there is no refuge from Allah (His seizing) except in Him, then Allah relented toward them, so that they might turn to Him. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.81: And the final message for everyone is this,
blocks.83: O believers! Fear Allah and be with the truthful.{{1}}
blocks.84: Talhah (RA) ran forward. The rest came later, slowly. Yet Ka‘b (RA) remembered that one for his whole life. For a person who returns after a mistake, could I ever be a Talhah? Not raising the mistake, only saying, it is good, you have come back. And Ka‘b’s (RA) truth. That is not the truth of one night. It is the resolve of the rest of life.
blocks.86: There was a man in Madinah named Abu ‘Amir. He had become a Christian and lived the life of a monk. Before the Prophet’s {{1}} arrival the people of Madinah revered him greatly. When the Prophet {{2}} came he invited him too to the truth. He did not accept. On the contrary he thought of him as his rival. From Badr to Hunayn he stood beside the disbelievers of Makkah. Seeing the Muslims’ victory at Hunayn he went off to Syria. From there he wrote a letter to the hypocrites of Madinah, organise yourselves, build a base, I am bringing the king of Rome. The base will be in the name of a mosque. Weapons will be stored there secretly, consultations will be held, when my men come they will stay there.{{3}}
blocks.87: In the area of Quba they raised a building. They came to the Prophet {{1}} and said, there are many weak people among us, the mosque of Quba is far. Please come and pray a little for us, we will gain blessing. The Prophet {{2}} was then in the preparation for Tabuk. He said, I am going to Tabuk now, on the way back, if Allah wills, I will go. On the return, at a place near Madinah called Dhu Awan, the verse was revealed. The Qur’an said,
blocks.89: And there are some who built a mosque with the purpose of causing harm (to the Muslims), speaking words of disbelief, creating division among the believers, and providing a base for the one who has been at war with Allah and His Messenger from before. They will certainly swear, we did it only with good intentions. But Allah bears witness that they are certainly liars.{{1}}
blocks.91: (O Prophet!) Never stand (for prayer) in that (that is, in that so-called mosque). But the mosque whose foundation was laid on taqwa from the first day is more deserving of your standing in it. In it are men who love to be pure. Allah loves those who are pure.{{1}}
blocks.92: The Prophet {{1}} sent Malik ibn Dukhshum and Ma‘n ibn ‘Adi (RA). They went and burned that base to ashes. Building is easy. Wrapping it in worship is easy too. There is only one question, on what is the foundation? Even today such ventures in the name of religion are seen, whose real work is division, factionalism, and a base against someone. With the mouth it is said, we did it with good intentions. The Qur’an’s answer is on that very oath: Allah bears witness, they are liars.

porbos.title: The Boundary of Mercy • Abu Bakr, Amir of Hajj • In Crowds • Dimam’s Questions • The Delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays • Tamim’s Raised Voices • The Lat of Thaqif • Najran and the Mubahalah • The Woman of al-Hirah • Musaylamah’s Claim • On the Road to Yemen • Final Word

blocks.1: What happened after the death of ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Ibn ‘Umar (RA) tells. His son came to the Prophet {{1}}, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abdillah, a sincere Muslim. He said, give me your shirt, I will shroud my father in it; and you lead the funeral prayer, ask forgiveness for him. The Prophet {{2}} gave his own shirt. He said, let me know, I will lead the prayer. When the time of the funeral came, the Prophet {{3}} went to lead it, ‘Umar (RA) pulled him back,
blocks.2: Has Allah not forbidden you to lead the funeral prayer of the hypocrites? The Prophet {{1}} said, I have been given the choice between two. He said, ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. He led the funeral prayer. Then it was revealed, when any of them dies you shall never lead the funeral prayer over him.{{2}}
blocks.3: The Qur’an then made it clear,
blocks.5: (O Prophet!) When any of them (that is, the hypocrites) dies, do not pray (the funeral prayer) over him, nor stand at his grave. They adopted a way of disbelief with Allah and His Messenger and died as transgressors.{{1}}
blocks.6: For his son’s sake the Prophet {{1}} did not turn away even an enemy’s funeral. It was a call of mercy. Then the verse came, he turned back, and never led it again. Mercy is right, but the boundary is Allah’s. Our soft heart often builds arguments, and we cross the limit. At the limit Allah has set, my compassion ends.
blocks.8: In the Hajj of 9 AH the Prophet {{1}} did not go himself. He sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) as amir. Abu Hurayrah (RA) says,
blocks.9: In that Hajj Abu Bakr sent me with some heralds to announce at Mina on the day of sacrifice: after this year no polytheist may perform Hajj, and no one may circumambulate the Ka‘bah naked.{{1}}
blocks.10: Then the Prophet {{1}} sent ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) after them, with the command to proclaim Surah Bara’ah. Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, ‘Ali proclaimed Bara’ah with us among the people of Mina on the day of sacrifice, and also proclaimed, after this year no polytheist will perform Hajj, and no one will circumambulate naked.{{2}}
blocks.11: In Jahiliyyah circumambulation around the Ka‘bah went on naked. The announcement was made: in this House there is no place for idols any more, nor for shamelessness.
blocks.13: After Tabuk the sky of Arabia changed. Tribe after tribe was sending delegations to Madinah. Historians have recorded the names of more than seventy delegations. At its root was a waiting. ‘Amr ibn Salimah (RA) says, we lived beside a water well, which was a thoroughfare for people. Caravans passed. We would ask, what has happened to the people? Who is this man? They would say, he claims Allah has sent him, has sent revelation. I would memorise those words, until it was as if they were fixed in my chest. He says further,
blocks.14: The Arabs were waiting for the conquest of Makkah to accept Islam. They would say, leave him and his people. If he prevails over them, he is a true prophet. When the conquest happened, every people rushed to Islam.{{1}}
blocks.15: The story of ‘Amr (RA) does not stop here. His father had become Muslim before the people. Returning from the Prophet {{1}} he said, by Allah, I have come from the true Prophet. He has said, such prayer at such time. When the time of prayer comes, one of you should call the adhan, and the one with the most Qur’an memorised should lead. ‘Amr (RA) says,
blocks.16: The people looked and found no one with more Qur’an memorised than me, because I had learned by listening to the caravans. So they pushed me forward. I was then six or seven years old.{{1}}
blocks.17: The qualification for leading prayer is not age but knowledge of the Qur’an. And there was one way of learning: to hold on to what reaches the ear. Verses flung from the mouths of passing caravans lodged in the chest of a six-year-old boy. Of what I hear in a day, how much do I hold on to?
blocks.19: In the mosque the Prophet {{1}} was sitting leaning among the Companions. Just then a man entered riding a camel. He made the camel kneel inside the mosque itself and tied it. He asked, which of you is Muhammad? The people said, that fair man there, sitting leaning. He said, the son of ‘Abd al-Muttalib? The Prophet {{2}} said, I have answered you. Anas (RA) says, the man then said to the Prophet {{3}},
blocks.20: I will question you, and I will make it hard. Do not take it to heart. The Prophet {{1}} said, ask whatever you wish.{{2}}
blocks.21: He asked, I ask you by the Lord of those before you, did Allah send you to all people? The Prophet {{1}} said, by Allah, yes. Did Allah command you the five daily prayers, by day and night? Yes. The fasting of this month? Yes. To take sadaqah from our rich and distribute it among our poor? Yes. Then he said, I believe in what you have brought. I am the envoy of my people. I am Dimam ibn Tha‘labah, a brother of Banu Sa‘d ibn Bakr.{{2}}
blocks.22: The Bedouin spoke roughly. He tied his camel in the mosque. He came forward and asked directly. The Prophet {{1}} did not frown. The reply was, ask whatever you wish. Today we set the worth of a question by the manner of the questioner. One who has come to know the truth will get an answer, whatever their manner.
blocks.24: From the direction of Bahrain came the delegation of the ‘Abd al-Qays tribe. Between them and Madinah were the disbelievers of the Mudar tribe, so coming was possible only in the sacred months. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says, the Prophet {{1}} asked them, who are you? They said, Rabi‘ah. He said,
blocks.25: Welcome to this delegation, who are neither humiliated nor regretful.{{1}}
blocks.26: They said, give us a clear instruction that we can tell to those behind us and by which we may enter Paradise if we follow it. The Prophet {{1}} commanded them four things and forbade four things. The first thing, faith in the one Allah, that is, to testify that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; then establishing prayer, zakah, fasting in Ramadan, and paying a fifth of the spoils. He forbade a few vessels used for making intoxicants. Then he said,
blocks.27: Keep these in memory, and tell those behind you.{{1}}
blocks.28: Not humiliated, not regretful. For those who have come, the very first word they heard is honour. What adjectives do we give to whom?
blocks.30: The Banu Tamim party came at midday. They did not know manners. Some of them began calling from outside the Prophet’s {{1}} house. Between Abu Bakr and ‘Umar (RA) talk arose about appointing an amir for the party. ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) says, when the caravan of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet {{2}},
blocks.31: Abu Bakr said, appoint al-Qa‘qa‘ ibn Ma‘bad as amir. ‘Umar said, no, appoint al-Aqra‘ ibn Habis. Abu Bakr said, you only want to oppose me. ‘Umar said, I did not want to oppose you. They argued, and both their voices rose.{{1}}
blocks.34: O believers! Do not go ahead (in any matter) of Allah and His Messenger. Fear Allah. Surely Allah hears everything, knows everything.{{1}}
blocks.36: O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become void without your knowing.{{1}}
blocks.38: After this verse ‘Umar used to speak with the Prophet {{1}} in such a low voice that he could not understand without asking again.{{2}}
blocks.39: Again some of Banu Tamim came and said, you have given glad tidings, now give us something. In the words there is no meaning of glad tidings, only asking. It showed on the Prophet’s {{1}} face. Then when a party from Yemen came he said, accept the glad tidings, since Banu Tamim did not. They said, we accept.{{2}}
blocks.40: Manners are not only inside prayer but in the voice. Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, the two best of men, had raised their voices in debate. The Qur’an warned. The language is very hard: your deeds will be void, without your knowing. Even with a good intention, raising the voice can bring that loss.
blocks.42: The story of Thaqif is a little different. Their leader ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud had gone back from the Prophet {{1}} with Islam. He thought his people would follow his word; he was the most obeyed chief of the people. The moment he called to Islam, arrows came from all sides. By that arrow he was martyred. After a few months they realised that all the surrounding tribes had become Muslim, fighting was no longer possible. So they sent a delegation. Ramadan of 9 AH. After returning, the delegates did not tell everything at first. On the contrary they frightened them, the Prophet {{2}} has told us to give up adultery, wine and usury, otherwise war. Two or three days passed. Allah poured fear into their hearts. They said, go back, accept. Then the delegates told the real matter openly, and all of Thaqif became Muslim.{{3}}
blocks.43: In that party was ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As (RA). He made a request to the Prophet {{1}},
blocks.44: O Messenger of Allah, make me the imam of my people. The Prophet {{1}} said, you are their imam. Follow the reckoning of the weakest among them, and take a muadhdhin who does not take payment for the adhan.{{2}}
blocks.45: To break the idol of al-Lat the Prophet {{1}} sent Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) with a party. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah (RA) came forward with a mace in hand and said, today I will make Thaqif laugh a little. Striking al-Lat, he himself fell to the ground writhing. The people of Thaqif cried out in terror, the goddess has killed him! Al-Mughirah (RA) leapt up and said, may Allah destroy you, this is only earth and stone! Then the walls were broken and levelled with the ground. From inside came out ornaments and clothing; the Prophet {{2}} distributed them that very day.{{3}}
blocks.46: The blow that fell on al-Lat fell on stone. But what was broken was something inside the mind. A whole tribe was waiting for someone to say, this is earth and stone. They knew, yet out of fear they would not touch it. Is there something like that in my house too? Something I know to be earth and stone, yet do not touch, thinking what will people say?
blocks.48: Seven stages from Makkah toward Yemen lies Najran. Seventy-three settlements. Nearly a hundred thousand fighters, all Christians. A delegation of sixty came. Their three leaders: the ‘Aqib ‘Abd al-Masih, the Sayyid Ayham, and the bishop Abu Harithah ibn ‘Alqamah. The Prophet {{1}} invited them to Islam, recited the Qur’an to them. They wanted to know the Prophet’s {{2}} view about ‘Isa (AS). The verse was revealed,{{3}}
blocks.50: To whoever disputes with you about this (the account of ‘Isa, AS) after the true knowledge that has come to you, say, come, let us call our children and your children, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves, then let us all humbly beseech Allah and send the curse of Allah upon the liars.{{1}}
blocks.51: The next morning at dawn the Prophet {{1}} came out. With him Hasan, Husayn, Fatimah and ‘Ali (RA). Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) says,
blocks.52: When Allah revealed this verse, ‘come, let us call our children’, the Prophet {{1}} called ‘Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn. He said, O Allah, these are my family.{{2}}
blocks.53: The two leaders of Najran were shaken. One said to the other, do not do it; if he is a prophet, neither we nor anyone after us will succeed. Hudhayfah (RA) says, they came and said, we will give you whatever you want, only send with us a trustworthy man. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.54: I will surely send with you a trustworthy man, one who is entirely trustworthy. The Companions all looked up. He said, stand, Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. When he stood the Prophet {{1}} said, this is the trustee of this ummah.{{2}}
blocks.55: Those who are certain of the truth do not fear to face a curse. Those who harbour doubt inwardly draw back at the last moment. To draw back from the place of Mubahalah is to admit one’s own doubt. And the title ‘Amin’. The first condition of responsibility is trust. All looked up eagerly, the Prophet {{1}} called a name. The one who seeks responsibility does not get it; the one who is worthy of trust is the one called.
blocks.57: ‘Adi ibn Hatim (RA) says, I was sitting with the Prophet {{1}}. One came and complained of poverty. Another came and complained of highway robbery. The Prophet {{2}} said, ‘Adi, have you seen al-Hirah? I said, I have not seen it, but I have heard of it. He said,
blocks.58: If your life is long, you will see a woman in a howdah travel from al-Hirah and circumambulate the Ka‘bah, fearing no one but Allah.{{1}}
blocks.59: ‘Adi (RA) says, I thought to myself, where will the robbers of the Tayy tribe be then? The Prophet {{1}} said further, the treasures of Kisra will be opened. ‘Adi (RA) says, I saw that woman. And I was among those who conquered the treasures of Kisra. To those who had come with complaints of poverty and robbery, the Prophet {{2}} did not give despair. He drew a picture ahead, of safety and prosperity. ‘Adi (RA) lived to see that picture with his own eyes. In answer to complaint, not despair but hope.
blocks.61: A party of Banu Hanifah came. Among them was Musaylamah. He lodged in the house of an Ansari. Coming to the Prophet {{1}} he first spoke of accepting Islam. But in him there were pride and greed for leadership. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says, he began saying, if Muhammad entrusts the charge to me after him, I will follow him. He had come with many men of his people. The Prophet {{2}} went toward him. With him Thabit ibn Qays (RA). In the Prophet’s {{3}} hand was a date-palm branch. Standing before Musaylamah he said,
blocks.62: If you asked me even for this piece of branch, I would not give it to you. What Allah has decreed for you, you cannot pass beyond. And if you turn away, Allah will destroy you. I see in you the very man I was shown in a dream.{{1}}
blocks.63: Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) wanted to know, what was the dream? Abu Hurayrah (RA) told, the Prophet {{1}} had said,
blocks.64: I was asleep. In the dream I saw two bracelets of gold on my two hands. I became worried. In the dream I was told, blow on them. I blew, and both flew away. I interpreted it: two liars will emerge after me; one al-‘Ansi, the other Musaylamah.{{1}}
blocks.65: Later Musaylamah claimed a share in prophethood, declared wine and adultery lawful for his people, and in the time of Abu Bakr (RA) was killed in the Battle of al-Yamamah. To seek prophethood as a share or an inheritance means making religion a ladder to power. The Prophet {{1}} himself went before him, with a companion, courteously; but in two sentences he drew the boundary. He did not open the door for one who asked for a share of power.{{2}}
blocks.67: Delegations are coming, and the Prophet {{1}} himself is sending teachers and governors. To Yemen went Mu‘adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA). Yemen was then in two parts. One part to one, the other part to the other. At the time of sending them off the Prophet {{2}} said to both,
blocks.68: Make things easy, do not make them hard. Give glad tidings, do not drive people away.{{1}}
blocks.69: To Mu‘adh (RA) he said still more, separately. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) narrates,
blocks.70: You are going to a people of the People of the Book. First invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they accept, inform them that Allah has made five prayers obligatory on them every day and night. If they accept, inform them that Allah has made sadaqah obligatory on them, to be taken from their rich and returned to their poor. If they accept, beware, do not take the best of their wealth; and fear the supplication of the wronged, for between it and Allah there is no veil.{{1}}
blocks.71: Three things for one who has gained power. Make things easy. Give good news. Fear the supplication of the wronged. For today’s administrator, manager, teacher, for all. And do not take the most beloved wealth. The collector’s hand usually lifts the best thing first. The Prophet {{1}} warned Mu‘adh (RA) against that temptation too.
blocks.73: Returning from Tabuk, then the flood of delegations; a few pictures of these few months stay in the mind. In the heat, before an eight-hundred-mile desert road, when the easiest thing was to say, not now. The tears of Abu Musa’s companions, in grief at not finding mounts. ‘Uthman’s lap full of dinars, Abu Bakr’s Allah and His Messenger. Abu ‘Aqil’s half sa‘. ‘Ali’s hurt and the answer of Harun and Musa. A base in the disguise of a mosque. The boundary of mercy. Then the delegations: Dimam, ‘Abd al-Qays, Tamim, Thaqif, Najran, ‘Adi. Musaylamah’s rejected claim. Mu‘adh, with Yemen’s road in his hands. Inside every picture a person, and one small question. Who is giving a valid excuse, who is arranging a pretext, people can never catch this difference. Allah can catch it, and one’s own heart can. So take one task from today’s dars.
blocks.75: Ka‘b (RA) could have given a false pretext, he did not; he bore fifty nights of hardship and spoke the truth, and that very truth saved him. Today I will ask myself one question: which sin or negligence have I still kept covered under a beautiful pretext, even from myself? Today, without any pretext, I will repent before Allah for that one sin, and from today I will never give up this habit of speaking the truth.

quiz.q: What lesson did the dars draw from the incident of Ibn Ubayy’s funeral?
o: Turning away an enemy’s son is the safe course
Shrouding is not permissible without the funeral prayer
Announcing the hypocrite’s name is necessary
Mercy is right, but the boundary is Allah’s

quiz.q: A friend’s father was an open enemy. The friend asked you to intercede for him. From the incident of Ibn Ubayy, what balance?
o: Remembering the enmity, I will turn him away directly and show no mercy
For mercy’s sake I will loosen the boundary
I will show mercy, but not cross Allah’s boundary
Stay silent and avoid the matter

quiz.q: In a village there is a six- or seven-year-old boy who knows the most Qur’an. According to the Prophet’s ﷺ guidance, who will lead the prayer?
o: The oldest and most experienced person of the village
The one with the most Qur’an memorised
The richest person
The most influential leader

quiz.q: A new student is asking hard questions in a rude manner. According to the incident of Dimam, what should the teacher do?
o: First teach manners, then listen to the question
Say, ask whatever you wish
Ask him to put the question later
Express annoyance and stop him

quiz.q: Before the teacher, two students raised their voices arguing over some matter. What is the teaching of al-Hujurat?
o: If the intention is good, raising the voice is not at all a fault
If the teacher is not present, there is no restriction
Only when losing in debate must the voice be lowered
Even with a good intention, raising the voice can bring harm

quiz.q: In a village everyone inwardly knows a superstition to be hollow, yet out of fear no one breaks it. With which incident of the dars does this match?
o: With the burning of the Mosque of Dirar
With the gathering of water at the spring of Tabuk
With the idol of al-Lat and the incident of al-Mughirah (RA)
With the quick passing by al-Hijr

quiz.q: What does the withdrawal of the Najran leaders from the place of Mubahalah indicate?
o: Admitting their own doubt
Yielding to a momentary fear
Having already accepted Islam
Disrespect toward the Prophet’s ﷺ family

quiz.q: What is the import of ‘If Muhammad entrusts the charge to me after him’?
o: Searching for the Prophet’s ﷺ successor
Eagerness to learn religious knowledge
Making prophethood a share of power
A sense of responsibility toward the people

quiz.q: A leader says, ‘if you give me the charge in the future, I will follow you.’ In the light of the reply the Prophet ﷺ gave Musaylamah, what does this show?
o: The door is not open for asking a share of power
Charge is gained by asking
Position is gained by first being obedient
Charge must be left behind for the next generation

quiz.q: A new official has been given the charge of government collection. In the light of the warning the Prophet ﷺ gave Mu‘adh, what should be done?
o: I will not choose the beloved wealth, I will fear the supplication of the wronged
I will take the most valuable thing first and keep it safe
I will collect by pressing everyone at an equal rate
I will keep all that is collected with myself
